text: Capsule says 'the law' without naming it; weak when quoted alone.
'The disclosure rules in the capsule above' is not self-contained if the paragraph is quoted.
'I'd want these answered first' uses a first-person voice with no established speaker.
Opening has no Northern California or Bay Area texture; acceptable for the opener, but local context must appear in later sections.
First-person 'the first question I ask' implies a personal practice not backed by an approved brand fact.
'the first question I ask' implies personal practice with no supporting brand fact or ledger claim.
The 'holder of title or authority has to sign' point is stated three to four times in one short section.
The line 'Here is who else can be affected, and why each one matters.' repeats the H3 and adds nothing.
No Northern California or Bay Area feel in this section.
Opening paragraph refers to 'the state statute' without naming H&S 17920.3 until the next paragraph.
The 'an official decides whether a home meets the conditions' point is made three times in one section.
H3 promises checks but the first two bullets read as descriptions of concerns.
"not whether to disclose" implies disclosure is always required despite the 1102.2 exception.
No internal link in this section; none is planned for it, so this is informational only.
Opening paragraph and the first bullet list state the same three legal points twice.
'Clearing the house out is your choice' is stated flat; a local enforcement notice could make cleanup not optional.
Opening sentence answers the H2 but not as a plain yes/no that is easy to quote.
Last bullet repeats itself: 'You would be trading some price for privacy and fewer showings.'
Last bullet repeats 'privacy and fewer showings' in two consecutive sentences.
Closing line 'spend money on a cleanout or on a sale' is vague and reads oddly.
Voice is competent but has little of Juan's 'real question / It depends' rhythm; 'Here is the law in plain terms' is generic.
Opening paragraph answers the H2 only indirectly; routes are not named until the H3s.
"Here is what the law says." is a stiff lead-in to the statute paragraph.
'It is the health officer or the fire official' names deciders that clm:1 (junk/debris) does not name.
'not you and not me' uses a first-person voice that may be inconsistent with the rest of the guide.
The So is / So is / And so is chain reads like a statute recital.
'Some of them can apply to a house with a lot of accumulated belongings' arrives before the hedge that the statute does not mention hoarding.
No mention of an occupant who is reluctant or not ready to leave.
Opening sentence omits the listing agent that the bullet list includes.
Opening is a bare list of professionals; lead with the homeowner's real question in Juan's stance.
Note says the guide explains what to ask, but the list gives topics, not questions.
Closing hand-off is correct and low-pressure but could show honest-options stance.
Item 6 says 'Sell directly to skip cleanout and showings'. It stays general and does not say Twin Home Buyer does this, so it is not a blocker. Keep it general and never tie it to THB.
Item 2 mentions authority and city or county notices but has no confirm-with-a-professional line. Items 3, 4 and 6 carry that language, so this passes.
Item 3 answer starts with 'It', which does not stand alone when quoted.
Item 4 answer starts with 'That depends...' and does not name who can sell in its first words.
Item 3 answer opens with 'It can look at the property.' with no clear antecedent.
Items 1 and 5 both restate the void-waiver point.
Answers are accurate but neutral; little of Juan's 'real question is' stance.
